entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zwentibold, a member of the Carolingian dynasty, was the illegitimate son of Emperor Arnulf. In 895, his father granted him the Kingdom of Lotharingia, which he ruled until his death on August 18, 900.


 Zwentibold was born into a prominent imperial family and played a significant role in the Carolingian Empire's decline. His reign was marked by struggles with neighboring kingdoms and a decline in the empire's power.


 Despite the challenges, Zwentibold's rule allowed the Kingdom of Lotharingia to maintain its independence and culture. His legacy serves as a reminder of the complexities of medieval politics and the impact of imperial succession on regional identities.


 The story of Zwentibold serves as a microcosm of the Carolingian Empire's trajectory, illustrating the tensions between imperial authority and regional autonomy in the Middle Ages.
